title: Midday inference triage catch-all — Miguel personal scratchpad
content:
---
Midday inference triage / catch-all (scratchpad)
Owner: Miguel Ortega  — quick notes to self, not polished
---

Context (today):
- Observed intermittent p99 token latency spikes in hosted region-us-east-1 around 12:15–12:45 UTC. Customer impact small but reproducible on a single shard group.
- Affected route: /v1/generate (model: smallish-example-7B-quant) — see INF-4872 for initial incident log.
- Working hypothesis: sudden KV cache eviction + a noisy background compaction job + batch scheduler head-of-line blocking.

Immediate triage checklist (fast):
- [x] Pull relevant logs from the timeframe (12:10–12:50 UTC).
  - cmd: kubectl -n inference logs $(kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=runtime -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}') -c runtime --since=60m | grep -E "evict|batch|latency|panic"
- [x] Check autoscaler events for any scale-up/scale-down that aligns with spike.
- [ ] Check node-level metrics on gpu-5 (temp, cuda-mig, iommu).
- [ ] Verify whether rolling deploy happened ~12:00 UTC (release-engineering / deploy tags).

Quick observations from logs (notes to self):
- Several "kv-cache: evict(prefix)" entries at 12:14:23 from pod runtime-5gx — pattern: burst of evict logs then p99 climb.
- Batch scheduler reported a single large batch (size 64) around 12:15; downstream kernel reported slower kernel-time for attention (see trace id 0x9f2b).
- One node reported an OOM-kill for a helper process 12:18 but main runtime stayed up (process restarted).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Eviction cascade: prefix cache eviction causes more cache misses, resulting in larger KV fetches and longer attention kernel runs.
2) Batch scheduler heuristic allowed a large batch that blocked small low-latency requests (HLB issue).
3) NUMA/cuda pinning issue on a single host causing variable kernel perf (suspect on gpu-5).

Quick experiments to run (low risk, ordered):
- Experiment A (read-only): enable prefix-cache-stats=verbose on the affected shard for 10m window. Observe hit/miss ratio. Expected: if hypothesis 1 true, miss rate spikes at 12:14 zone.
  - runtime flag: --kv-prefix-stats=verbose
  - telemetry: prefix_hits, prefix_misses, avg_fetch_size
  - rollback: revert flag after 10m
- Experiment B (scheduler tweak, canary): temporarily set max_batch_size=32 for one canary node pool. If p99 drops for that pool, indicates scheduler batch sizing issue.
  - rollout: canary 2 nodes, 10m evaluation
  - metrics: p50/p90/p99, batch_size_distribution
- Experiment C (node hold): cordon gpu-5 for new allocations and observe whether p99 for shard group normalizes within 15m.

Runbook snippets / commands to paste in incident channel:
- Fetch evict trace: kubectl -n inference logs <pod> -c runtime --since=30m | grep evict | sed -n '1,200p'
- Scheduler metric query (prom): sum(rate(runtime_scheduler_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le)
- Node perf dump: ssh perf@gpu-5 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,clocks.sm --format=csv -l 2 --display=MEMORY' (run during repro)

Notes to self on debugging kernel traces:
- When looking at kernel timeline, pay attention to small high-latency kernels during large-batch invocations — sometimes memory thrash causes per-invocation regression instead of mean.
- Save a sample of KV payload that triggers large fetch (anonymize customer data) for offline profiling.

Outstanding questions / follow-ups:
- Why did eviction burst start exactly at 12:14? Check LRU window and any background eviction cron jobs (storage compaction).
- Was there a correlated traffic pattern (one customer sending many long-context requests) — ask CS to check recent top-requests.
- Do we have a recent roll of the kernel library on that node group? (check GH PR list and deploy tags)
- If experiment B helps, revisit scheduler heuristic (maybe add weight for low-latency routes).

To-dos (short-term):
- [ ] Run Experiment A on affected shard (Miguel) — estimate 10–15m.
- [ ] Post quick findings to #runtime-ops and tag Priya/Noah.
- [ ] If A supports eviction hypothesis, schedule a follow-up to increase default prefix cache size for that model in staging.
- [ ] If B helps, open design doc for revised batching heuristic (start draft: /confluence/kernel-batching-notes).
- [ ] Capture anonymized KV sample and attach to INF-4872.

To-dos (longer):
- [ ] Add a telemetry alert for sudden prefix_miss_rate > 10% in 5m window (owner: infra-metrics).
- [ ] Add a canary test that fires mixed-size requests and asserts p99 < 300ms under modest load.

Random scratch / ideas (brain dump):
- Consider adding "batch preemption" for low-latency requests: allow scheduler to preempt a queued large batch if X% of waiting items are marked low-latency. Risk: complexity.
- Investigate whether we can do async KV prefetch for requests predicted to expand context — would reduce synchronous fetch penalty but increases memory.

Notes to self before lunch:
- Save samples, run A, post interim note, then step away. If things escalate, escalate to Priya and SRE.

END
